name: Rope
overview: Scripture uses the image of rope both literally and figuratively to convey themes of servitude, trial, and strength. Ropes worn on the head symbolized humility and submission, as seen when servants put ropes on their heads as an emblem of servitude before a king (1 Kings 20:31-32). Figuratively, ropes represent the bonds of affliction and temptation that can ensnare the wicked (Job 36:8; Proverbs 5:22), and the psalmist describes cords as snares set by the proud (Psalms 140:5). Yet, the strength of a threefold cord also illustrates the power of unity and resilience, not easily broken (Ecclesiastes 4:12).
